title: status
description: What a session's context window is doing, written on every render and left at a predictable path keyed by session. An agent cannot measure its own context: the numbers arrive in the payload the status line is handed and nothing else in the session sees them, so a reader that would otherwise tail a transcript and sum usage records reads this instead. Held here rather than in wrench's shipped set: bin/board is the only consumer, which makes this infobot's contract with one reader rather than a word in the bolt/wrench/toolbox vocabulary. See wrench's docs/DECISIONS/what-earns-a-place-in-the-shipped-set.md, part 3.

session.description: The session this describes, which is also what names the file. A reader knowing its own session id knows where to look and needs to know nothing else.

written.description: When the render that produced this happened. A reader finding a file for a session that has ended has no other way to tell a live measurement from one left behind.

cwd.description: Where the session is working. Absent rather than empty when the payload did not say, so a reader tells 'not said' from 'said to be nothing'.

model.description: The model's display name, or its id when there is no display name. Absent when the payload carried neither.

effort.description: The effort level the session is running at. Absent when the payload did not carry one.

context_used.description: Tokens the window holds, counted on the input side alone. The output side is not part of what a window is full of.

context_size.description: The window's capacity as the payload reported it, rather than a constant per model, because the same model runs at more than one size.

context_remaining.description: Derived rather than read, and never negative: a payload reporting more used than the window holds gives zero here. A negative would read as a bug in whatever drew it.

context_percent.description: How full the window is, neither floored nor capped, so a reader sees an over-full window as over-full where a bar can only draw it as full. Type is all a schema can say: that the spelling carries a decimal point and never an exponent is the encoder's guarantee, and it matters because a reader matching digits against 1e+06 captures 1, which is a plausible small number rather than a parse failure.
